claims.text: What the image looks like Diffuse small + large bowel dilation, no transition, post-op → paralytic ileus
claims.quote: Diffuse small + large bowel dilation, no transition, post-op Paralytic ileus

claims.text: As in obstruction, films show gaseous distention of isolated segments of intestine; in postoperative ileus gas may accumulate more in the colon than in the small bowel
claims.quote: In both conditions, abdominal radiographs show gaseous distention of isolated segments of intestine. In postoperative ileus, however, gas may accumulate more in the colon than in the small bowel.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Small bowel: central; valvulae conniventes cross the full lumen; dilated > 3 cm
claims.quote: small bowel = central, valvulae conniventes cross full lumen, dilated >3 cm.

claims.text: Large bowel: peripheral “picture frame”; haustra do NOT cross the full diameter; dilated > 6 cm (> 9 cm at the cecum)
claims.quote: Large bowel = peripheral 'picture frame', haustra do NOT cross full diameter, dilated >6 cm (>9 cm at cecum).

claims.text: Postoperative gas in the small bowel often implies a complication (eg, obstruction, peritonitis)
claims.quote: Postoperative accumulation of gas in the small bowel often implies development of a complication (eg, obstruction, peritonitis).

claims.text: Films can look like obstruction (hard to tell apart unless clinical features clearly favor one); contrast-enhanced CT may help differentiate and suggest a cause
claims.quote: Sometimes, radiographic findings are similar to those of intestinal obstruction; differentiation can be difficult unless clinical features clearly favor one or the other. A contrast-enhanced CT may help differentiate between the two and suggest an underlying cause of the ileus.

claims.text: Causes A temporary arrest of peristalsis, most commonly after abdominal surgery, particularly when the intestines were manipulated
claims.quote: Ileus is a temporary arrest of intestinal peristalsis. It occurs most commonly after abdominal surgery, particularly when the intestines have been manipulated.

claims.text: Other causes: intraperitoneal or retroperitoneal inflammation (appendicitis, diverticulitis, perforated duodenal ulcer); retroperitoneal or intra-abdominal hematomas (ruptured AAA, blunt trauma); metabolic disturbances (hypokalemia); medications (opioids, anticholinergics, sometimes calcium channel blockers); sometimes renal or thoracic disease (lower rib fractures, lower lobe pneumonias, MI)
claims.quote: Intraperitoneal or retroperitoneal inflammation (eg, appendicitis, diverticulitis, perforated duodenal ulcer) Retroperitoneal or intra-abdominal hematomas (eg, from ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, blunt abdominal trauma) Metabolic disturbances (eg, hypokalemia) Medications (eg, opioids, anticholinergics, sometimes calcium channel blockers) Sometimes renal or thoracic disease (eg, lower rib fractures, lower lobe pneumonias, myocardial infarction)

claims.text: After surgery: the small bowel typically recovers within hours; stomach emptying is usually impaired for approximately 24 hours or more; the colon is often most affected and may stay inactive for 48 to 72 hours or more
claims.quote: The small bowel is typically least affected, with motility and absorption returning to normal within hours after surgery. Stomach emptying is usually impaired for approximately 24 hours or more. The colon is often most affected and may remain inactive for 48 to 72 hours or more.

claims.text: Symptoms Abdominal distention, nausea, vomiting and vague discomfort; pain rarely has the colicky pattern of mechanical obstruction; there may be obstipation or slight amounts of watery stool
claims.quote: Symptoms and signs of ileus include abdominal distention, nausea, vomiting, and vague discomfort. Pain rarely has the classic colicky pattern present in mechanical bowel obstruction. There may be obstipation or passage of slight amounts of watery stool.

claims.text: Silent abdomen or minimal peristalsis; not tender unless the underlying cause is inflammatory
claims.quote: Auscultation reveals a silent abdomen or minimal peristalsis. The abdomen is not tender unless the underlying cause is inflammatory.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: supportive (correct K+/Mg, hold opiates)
Continuous nasogastric suction, nothing by mouth, IV fluids and electrolytes, minimal sedatives, and no opioids or anticholinergics; keeping serum potassium > 4 mEq/L is especially important
claims.quote: Treatment of ileus involves continuous nasogastric suction, nothing by mouth, IV fluids and electrolytes, a minimal amount of sedatives, and avoidance of opioids and anticholinergic medications. Maintaining an adequate serum potassium level (> 4 mEq/L [> 4.00 mmol/L]) is especially important.

claims.text: Ileus persisting > 1 week probably has a mechanical obstructive cause; consider laparotomy
claims.quote: Ileus persisting > 1 week probably has a mechanical obstructive cause, and laparotomy should be considered.

claims.text: Colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome): colonoscopic decompression helps; some clinicians use IV neostigmine (requires cardiac monitoring)
claims.quote: Colonoscopic decompression is helpful in treating pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome), which consists of apparent obstruction at the splenic flexure, although no cause can be found by contrast enema or colonoscopy for the failure of gas and feces to pass this point. Some clinicians use IV neostigmine (which requires cardiac monitoring) to treat Ogilvie syndrome.
